messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Tenant aurelia-health (Dedicated pool eu-west-2) hitting sustained queue depth >100, p95 gen latency >= 2.8s, increase in 500s from model runtime. Pager triggered at 1912345678.
Maya Rao: I'm on it, paging Sanjay. tagging @Sanjay for scheduler/max_batch_tokens knobs. quick summary: dedicated pool, tenant-level shaper seems saturated.
Sanjay Patel: looking. seeing a lot of small requests + some long prefixes; current tenant config: max_batch_tokens=4096, scheduler_weight=0.4, max_concurrency=24. queue_depth per-replica ~ 30 -> 120 across 4 replicas.
Alex Chen: logs show KV cache misses climbing after 15:20z, plus a tail of >1s generation calls. suspect batching inefficiency + some bursty large-context requests.
Maya Rao: can we temporarily bump max_batch_tokens and reduce scheduler_weight to favor latency? Sanjay, what's safe?
Sanjay Patel: plan: 1) set max_batch_tokens=8192 2) set scheduler_weight=0.6 (favor filling bigger batches) 3) reduce max_concurrency to 18 to avoid head-of-line blocking. That should drop queue depth and p95. Applying now.
Sanjay Patel: running command: ```redwoodctl tenant update --tenant aurelia-health --max_batch_tokens 8192 --scheduler_weight 0.6 --max_concurrency 18```
deploy-bot: apply / started rollout of tenant config update (aurelia-health) on Dedicated eu-west-2. rollout id: r-20260315-42.
Sanjay Patel: change applied on 4/4 replicas. Watching metrics (queue_depth, p95, 500s).
Claire Gomez: I'll take the handoff if this persists into the night. Claire oncall in 25m.
Maya Rao: Customer impact: 2 customers on affected routes seeing increased tail latency & occasional 502s. CS alerted. L2 Support on thread: @L2 Support please collect request ids for any 502s so we can correlate.
L2 Support: copying logs, sending sample request ids: req_abc123, req_def456, req_ghi789. forwarding to customer-facing Slack.
Sanjay Patel: early signals: queue_depth total dropped from 118 -> 22 within 90s, p95 decreased from 2.9s -> 0.65s, 500s count fell by 85%. good initial effect.
Alex Chen: also turned on tenant-level prefix caching for the heavy endpoints (feature_toggle: tenant_prefix_cache=true). reduced repeated KV fetches. command: ```redwoodctl config set --tenant aurelia-health --key tenant_prefix_cache --value true```
Maya Rao: nice. Any risk from larger max_batch_tokens w.r.t memory or OOM?
Sanjay Patel: we're inside safety margin on 3090-like instances; memory headroom ~ 36%. will keep an eye. If we see OOM risk, rollback to 6144.
deploy-bot: monitor: alert if any replica reports oom_kill or model process restart.
Claire Gomez: I'm taking this into the night. next steps: 1) keep bespoke knobs for 2h, 2) schedule a short canary to gradually revert to default once traffic normalizes, 3) follow-up postmortem + customer async note. I'll onboard @Alex on the PM.
Maya Rao: logging actions for incident ticket INC-2026-348 on ops.impact. Recording mitigations and timings.
Sanjay Patel: adding a temporary tenant shaper rule to isolate aurelia-health from bursty cross-tenant interference: ```rctl shaper add --tenant aurelia-health --type token_bucket --rate 5000 --burst 15000 --reason "incident mitigation"```
Alex Chen: cpu/mem graphs look nominal after change. also set a short-lived routing fallback to a lighter model variant for long-context requests: ```routingctl set --tenant aurelia-health --fallback-model gpt-lite-8k --max_tokens_fallback 2048```
Maya Rao: customer ops update scheduled in 30m. Claire will handle the text to send.
L2 Support: forwarded correlated req ids to SRE, keeping CS informed.
Claire Gomez: handover notes: current knobs = max_batch_tokens 8192, scheduler_weight 0.6, max_concurrency 18, tenant_prefix_cache=true. monitor window until 1912346038 then consider gradual rollback if stable. 👍
Maya Rao: thanks all. if any degradation re-paging will go to primary oncall @Sanjay then to Claire.
oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged by Maya Rao, status: mitigated (evidence: p95 down, queue depth reduced). closing immediate pager; keep thread active for postmortem.
Sanjay Patel: will follow up with a short runbook snippet for future similar tenant spikes (include checks: queue_depth/replica, kv_cache_hit_ratio, model memory headroom, command snippets).
Maya Rao: filing postmortem draft after shift. tagging for follow-up: @Alex for graphs, @Claire for customer note, @Sanjay for runbook.
Claire Gomez: copying final metrics snapshot here: queue_depth: baseline 12, peak 118, post-change 18; p95: baseline 0.55s, peak 2.9s, post-change 0.65s; 500s: peak 42 -> 6. Will write follow-up.
Maya Rao: resolved for now. keeping incident open for root cause until postmortem. Thanks team :heart:
